applies_to: Eaton Powerware 9390 three-phase UPS systems on Modbus, read by a BASgatewayLX.
summary: Gateway profile for the Eaton Powerware 9390: 421 objects (80 AI, 341 BI), 98 polled by default. Binary inputs give the operating mode (on battery, on bypass, system normal, UPS off), breaker and module states and hundreds of alarm bits; analog inputs give battery voltage, % left and runtime, bypass, input and output voltages and load currents. There are no outputs.
notes: Built from Contemporary Controls' BASgatewayLX Modbus device profile Eaton_Powerware_9390_UPS_a_LX.csv; the profile maps the registers in the Powerware 9390 Modbus register list (https://www.ccontrols.com/support/dp/1391F-Modbus_Reg_Map-Rel.pdf).
Object instances are the ones this profile assigns when it is loaded into the gateway. A site that edited or rebuilt the profile may use different instances.
Only 98 of the 421 rows are flagged for polling in the profile; the rest are served only after you tick them in the gateway. Their descriptions say "not polled by default".

The CSV has no read/write column: Analog/Binary Inputs are read-only and Analog/Binary Outputs are commandable (priority array), which is how the gateway maps them (access inferred). Descriptions give the Modbus register each object reads.
Some names appear more than once in the profile as published (Rectifier Status); they are kept as printed and told apart by instance.

integration.summary: Read System Normal, On Battery, On Bypass, % battery left and runtime, and the key alarms.
setup: The BASgatewayLX presents each Modbus device as its own virtual BACnet device on BACnet IP; give it a unique device instance and Modbus address (serial) or IP address (Modbus TCP) when you add it with this profile.
One BASgatewayLX handles up to 100 Modbus devices and 1000 polled points in total, so leave unneeded rows unpolled.
gotchas: Unpolled rows do not appear as BACnet objects until enabled in the gateway's device profile page.
